headline.t: Your outbound engineer req has been open
. The system it describes ships in

intro: Your JD calls for one of the most advanced outbound engines in the world: Apollo for data, Clay for the workflow, HubSpot and Salesforce as the CRM spine, and a path from 5k to 250k emails a month. The system is well specified. The gap is that nobody is building it while you recruit. I build exactly this, fractionally. Here is the system I would ship for GetWing.

chain.d: ICP accounts and contacts pulled by API
Enrich, verify, score ICP fit, personalize
Dedupe vs CRM, route by fit and intent

build.outputsLabel: SHIPS TO THE TOOLS YOUR TEAM ALREADY USES

steps.p: Apollo company and contact data into Clay tables, plus web scraping for technographics and job-posting signals that show an automation need. LeadMagic and BounceBan verification run before anything touches a domain.

Clay normalizes size and industry, dedupes against HubSpot, applies weighted ICP scoring, then webhook-routes each record to the right destination. Low-fit and undeliverable records drop to suppression, not to your reps.

A daily cohort of scored, enriched, personalized leads auto-loads into Instantly with persona-mapped copy variants. Reply intent lands in a HubSpot dashboard for AE pickup. No manual list pulls, no spreadsheet handoffs.

timeline.p: Apollo into Clay, verification stack, ICP scoring logic. First scored records visible.
Routing rules, CRM dedupe, Instantly domain pools, persona copy variants.
Live daily cohort and reply dashboard, plus a handover doc so your team owns it.

outcomes.d: Not in six months when the seat fills. The engine works while you keep recruiting.
Deliverability and domain rotation are built in, not bolted on after the bounce rate spikes.
Every open, reply, and meeting tied to the account in HubSpot, not a spreadsheet.

proof.cap: Account-to-Outbound: an engine I built end to end, enriching 11,000 accounts with 93.9% verified contacts and routing them into live outbound.

ask.t: Three weeks. One working system. Fractional.
ask.p: I build the account-to-outbound engine your JD describes, live in three weeks, while you keep recruiting the full-time hire. If it works, we talk about what is next. If it does not, you keep the system and we part cleanly. No vendor process, no tool rollout, no long contract.
